title: Shepherd's herding dog: dielectrophoretic placement of nanowire access transistors
idea: A sheepdog drives sheep into pens. Grow doped core-shell Si nanowire transistors in bulk in a tube furnace, suspend them in liquid, and use AC dielectrophoresis on electrode pairs to herd one wire onto each site of a pre-built capacitor array.
why: Decouples a single-crystal access transistor from the capacitor substrate and removes epitaxy and transistor litho from the array. Furnace plus wet bench suits a small team (Facts 2, 3).

title: Bank-switchable floating body: dynamic mode or self-held bipolar latch
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: the same 3D floating-body tiers run in two modes set per bank by source-line bias. At low bias they are dense dynamic cells that need refresh; above the parasitic-BJT latch threshold, impact-ionization feedback holds 1 and 0 statically, so hot banks skip refresh and idle banks drop to near-zero bias.
why: Fact 3: per-bank choice between refresh-free static operation (+10-20% bandwidth) and minimum standby power with no capacitor and no extra transistor.

title: Phosphorus delta-doped epitaxial sheets serve as built-in buried bitlines
idea: In a monolithic Si epi tier stack, grow each horizontal bitline as an in-situ phosphorus-doped (>1e20) epitaxial sheet that the slit etch later segments into short local bitlines, so the bitline is a crystalline conductor formed during growth rather than metal pushed into 100:1 lateral cavities.
why: Removes the hardest metal fill of vertical-wordline 3D DRAM (fact 2) and its tungsten; the bitline self-aligns to its transistor tier, saving a critical mask per tier group.

title: Cubic mats with sense amplifiers at the array centroid tier
idea: Build each mat as a 64x64x64 cube instead of a 512x512 square and place its sense amps and local I/O in the middle tier, so every cell is at most 32 lateral pitches plus 32 tier pitches from its amplifier.
why: Energy per bit moved scales with wire length: mean path grows as N^(1/3) in 3D versus N^(1/2) in 2D, so for a 256 kb mat intra-mat wiring CV^2 drops ~5-8x (facts 5, 10) and bitline capacitance falls with it, relaxing required Cs.

title: Stencil-indexed deposition builds the 3D staircase, replacing trim-etch loops
idea: Substitute the staircase made by dozens of resist-trim + oxide/nitride fluorocarbon etch loops with deposition-defined steps: sputter an oxide-semiconductor/Mo/Al2O3 tier stack through a stepper-indexed stencil whose aperture edges move inward ~0.5 um per tier at each staircase site, so every tier terminates at its own offset; stencils are swapped and stripped in oxalic acid/H2O2.
why: 3D DRAM staircase cost (fact 2): eliminates ~N/2 litho-trim-etch cycles and all their fluorocarbon use; staircase becomes native to deposition.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall crossbars in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Domain-wall conduction: in LNOI wafers, which photonics fabs already make, voltage pulses create or erase conductive domain walls across each nanocell. Reading senses wall current without switching, so the read is non-destructive and the walls persist with no power.
why: Gives a non-volatile cell with non-destructive read (fact 8) and high endurance, stackable by wafer bonding (fact 2); claim >1e10 cycles and selector-friendly on/off >1e3.

title: Array-logic-array sandwich: each sense amp reads both bond faces
idea: IFR: 'periphery is free because every sense amp serves twice.' Backward: hybrid-bond array wafers to both the front and the thinned back of one logic wafer; each sense amp takes its true bitline from the top array and its reference bitline from the mirror cell in the bottom array (an open-bitline pair split across the stack), alternating roles per access.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): halves sense amps per bit with matched noise cancellation; ~25% bit-cost cut claimed.

title: Freight consolidation hub: base die sorts requests by row
idea: Like a cross-dock that fills containers before shipping, a 32 MB SRAM queue in the HBM/3D base die holds ~50k pending requests, radix-sorts them by row in hardware and fires an activation only when 32+ lines for that row are waiting or a deadline expires.
why: Activation amortization (fact 8): each activation serves 32-64 useful lines instead of 1-2 for random traffic; claims ~10x lower energy per access on latency-tolerant AI and graph workloads.

title: Wavelength-addressed tiers: color-coded phototransistor tier select
idea: Like wavelength-division multiplexing in fibre, give each tier's select transistors a different absorber bandgap (graded SiGe or tuned quantum dots) and light the stack through an in-plane waveguide grid at one wavelength, so only that tier's selectors turn on and no staircase or per-tier decoder is needed.
why: 3D staircase and periphery (facts 2, 7): staircase area goes to zero for 16-32 tiers and tier decoding moves off-die into a tunable laser.

title: Jelly-roll capacitor: strained bilayer self-rolls into a multi-turn spiral
idea: Borrow battery-cell winding: deposit a flat TiN/high-k/TiN/strained-SiN film beside each access transistor, release a sacrificial underlayer so built-in strain rolls it into a 3-5 turn Swiss roll standing on its anchor, multiplying plate area by the number of turns without any high-aspect-ratio etch.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): area comes from turns, not aspect ratio; three turns of a 300 nm-wide film give ~2-3x the area of a 60:1 pillar per footprint, enabling Cs >10 fF. Rolled MIM tubes exist at micron scale; nanoscale rolling uniformity is the risk.

title: Apollo restart protection: recompute tensors instead of storing them perfectly
idea: Revive the Apollo guidance computer's restart groups, which recovered from faults by re-running from checkpoints: data in 1%-BER 3D memory carry a light detection code, and on a detected-uncorrectable error the runtime recomputes that tensor tile from its producer kernel instead of relying on heavy ECC.
why: Cuts code overhead to ~3% and admits marginal cells; recompute is cheap for activations and KV pages, raising usable capacity.

title: Contactless whole-wafer self-test keeps test cost flat at 10x bits
idea: Worse: probe-test 10x more bits per die serially so test time and probe-card capex scale 10x. Flip: power every die on the wafer inductively or through on-die photovoltaic pads, run built-in self-test of all tiers in parallel, read pass/fail maps through an optical or RF backchannel, and program tier and row spares in the same pass.
why: Test (~5-10% of DRAM cost) stays flat while bits per die grow 10x, so the density gain is not eaten by test capex (capital intensity).

title: Fluorine-free-release nanoimprint replaces EUV on periodic array layers
idea: Substitute EUV exposures of the strictly periodic array layers (active, buried WL, BL, landing pad) with jet-and-flash nanoimprint, replacing the fluorinated anti-stick template silane (FDTS/FOTS) with a self-releasing siloxane-methacrylate resist plus a renewable water-soluble PVA release film and radical (PAG-free) UV cure.
why: EUV is one supplier and DRAM needs 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4): NIL is ~1/3-1/5 the capex per layer, buildable in the U.S., and the PFAS-free release removes NIL's own fluorine dependence.

title: Octopus-arm ganglia: thin-film decoders inside each tier shrink staircases
idea: Like octopus arms running local ganglia, deposit a small oxide-TFT row decoder at each tier's edge so the vertical staircase carries only ~10 predecoded address and power lines per tier group instead of one contact per wordline per tier, with the CMOS 'brain' below sending compact commands.
why: 3D staircase area grows with tier count and can take 10-20% of the die; local decoders shrink it ~5-10x, raising array efficiency and allowable tier count.

title: Stereocilia tip-link NEMS switches as zero-leak access devices
idea: Like hair-cell stereocilia whose tip links open channels only when deflected, make each access device a vertical nano-cantilever that electrostatically bends to touch the storage-node contact only when its wordline plane is energized; the air gap gives truly zero off-state leakage in a 3D vertical array.
why: Leakage tail forces refresh: a physical gap removes subthreshold and GIDL leakage so retention is set by the capacitor dielectric (minutes to hours), cutting refresh energy ~99%; contact endurance is the main risk.

title: 4H-SiC vertical-pillar DRAM: wide gap kills refresh, shrinks capacitor
idea: Inverts 'DRAM must be built in silicon.' Make 4F² vertical-pillar access transistors and trench capacitors in 4H-SiC (3.26 eV gap), where thermal leakage falls by many orders of magnitude, so retention runs to minutes and Cs can shrink ~10x.
why: Facts 1 and 3: refresh nearly vanishes and capacitor AR collapses from ~70:1 to ~7:1; taps U.S. SiC wafer capacity built for power devices.

title: Carbon-mandrel, titania-alumina spacers replace fluorocarbon quadruple patterning
idea: Substitute oxide-spacer/fluorocarbon SAQP with an ashable/chlorinable set: amorphous-carbon mandrels (O2 ash), ALD TiO2 first spacers and ALD Al2O3 second spacers etched with Cl2/BCl3 at >20:1 mutual selectivity, printed with a non-fluorinated PAG (sulfonium camphorsulfonate) resist, so ~16 nm pitch uses only O2, Cl2, BCl3 and HBr.
why: Litho capital and fluorine dependence (fact 4): ArF + SAQP array lines without EUV, fluorocarbon spacer etches, or PFAS photoacid generators.

title: Coaxial cable: grounded sleeves around every vertical bitline
idea: Adapted from coax: each vertical bitline in a 3D array is wrapped in a thin grounded metal sleeve over low-k, trading ~20% more self-capacitance for near-zero coupling to neighbor bitlines and plates.
why: Coupling noise ~-80% allows open-bitline 4F2 3D arrays without folded/twisted schemes and smaller sense margins (fact 1).

title: Sacrificial-polymer air-gap bitlines halve bitline capacitance
idea: Under 400 C, fill between bitlines with a polynorbornene-type sacrificial polymer, cap it with porous ALD SiO2, and decompose it through the cap at 350 C to leave air gaps. This works only because no later step needs high temperature.
why: Facts 1 and 10: about 35-45% lower Cb, so Cs can drop by the same fraction or bitline voltage swing can fall.

title: Vertical bucket brigade: charge hops tier-to-tier down to one sense tier
idea: Take the astronomy CCD and rotate its shift axis to vertical: stacked storage tiers linked by gated vertical channels clock charge packets down plane by plane to a single bottom tier of sense amps, so 64 storage tiers need no periphery of their own. Time split: dense tiers hold charge for ms, and a whole-plane shift takes ns per hop.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7), and per-tier wordline and sense wiring blocks 3D (fact 2); one sense tier for 64 storage tiers could cut periphery area per bit by >10x.

title: Shingled roof: TSV-free 3DS DDR5 via printed staircase edge traces
idea: Roof shingles overlap in steps: stack 4-8 DDR5 dies offset by 150 um in a staircase, and aerosol-jet or EHD-print 10-20 um silver traces down the exposed step edges to link each die's pads to the substrate in place of TSVs. The result is a standard 3DS DDR5 RDIMM device with an unchanged interface.
why: TSV tax (fact 6) for high-capacity server memory: no TSV area, keep-out or TSV yield loss; claim die area -6-8% and 3DS stack cost -20%.

title: Puff-pastry lamination: binary-tree bonding of mature-node DRAM wafers
idea: Laminated dough multiplies layers by folding; hybrid-bond pairs of thinned 2x-nm DRAM wafers face to face, then bond pairs of pairs, so a 16-tier stack needs only 4 serial bond-and-thin steps run in parallel on existing bonding and grinding tools, with relaxed 10 um edge TSVs.
why: 16x bits per footprint with zero new lithography (fact 4), using fully depreciated 2x-nm DRAM fabs and OSAT tools; serial cycle time scales as log2(N) and every tier is pre-tested.

title: Hot-embossed polymer trenches give 3D capacitors without plasma etch
idea: Emboss 5:1 trenches at 1 um pitch into a COC or polyimide web with a nickel-shim roller, conformally coat metal/AlOx/metal by spatial ALD and fill with printed conductor, giving each cell a folded capacitor.
why: Area multiplication is ~1+2*AR, so ~10x capacitor area per footprint from one roller pass: ~80 fF per 1 um^2 cell or 8 fF in 0.1 um^2, the 3D capacitor that wafer fabs must etch at 60-75:1 (fact 1).

title: Butterfly-wing gyroid electrodes replace 70:1 capacitor pillars
idea: Copy the gyroid networks in butterfly wing scales: spin a gyroid-forming triblock copolymer into a 400 nm layer over the storage contacts, remove one network, ALD TiN/high-k/TiN through the periodic 3D labyrinth, then cut it per cell with a coarse self-aligned grid so each storage node owns a gyroid block.
why: Capacitor charge wall: a 20 nm-period gyroid has ~10x the area per volume of a cylinder, giving ~5 fF in a 400 nm-tall structure (AR ~20:1 instead of 70:1) and ending pillar collapse.

title: Eliminate copper damascene: subtractive molybdenum array wiring
idea: Pattern bitlines and local interconnect by dry etching a blanket molybdenum film (with self-aligned dry-etched vias) instead of copper electroplating plus CMP, removing plating baths, slurry and post-CMP brush cleans.
why: Water: metal ECD and CMP are among the most water-intensive steps; subtractive Mo is fully dry and also avoids copper diffusion barriers at narrow pitch.

title: Nano-MLCC cells: deposited multilayer capacitor with side terminations
idea: Inverts 'capacitor plate area is set by etch depth.' Deposit N alternating electrode/dielectric films, cut cells, and contact alternate electrodes from two side vias like a ceramic MLCC termination, so plate area grows with layer count on a flat footprint.
why: Fact 1: a 10-layer stack gives ~10x plate area per footprint with no high-AR etch; capacitance scales with deposition cycles instead of AR 115.

title: On-chip MLCC: interleaved deposited electrodes replace deep capacitor etch
idea: [Box: multilayer interdigitated MIM | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | blanket ALD/PVD TiN/Ru/ZrO2 multilayer + selective lateral recess] Deposit N alternating TiN and Ru electrode sheets separated by ZrO2, etch one coarse pillar per cell, then selectively recess the Ru from one sidewall and the TiN from the other so storage node and plate interleave like a ceramic MLCC.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): capacitance scales with deposited layer count, not aspect ratio or lithography; ~10 sheets reach >5 fF at moderate AR.

title: Shingled die staircase with vertical bond-via wires replacing TSVs
idea: Fuse NAND-style offset die stacking with free-standing vertical copper wire arrays (US-developed bond-via-array): each DRAM die is shifted to expose an edge pad row and molded ~50 um-pitch vertical Cu wires rise from the substrate to every die, built on Arizona OSAT lines.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSVs, keep-out zones or TSV yield loss, recovering much of HBM's ~3x area-per-bit penalty; stack cost ~30% lower at ~3x DDR5 package bandwidth.

title: Arrays on both wafer faces share one sandwiched periphery layer
idea: Substitute the dead silicon bulk with a second array: build the 1T1C array and periphery on the front, bond to carrier, thin to ~1 um, then build a second low-temperature oxide-semiconductor 1T1C array on the backside (backside-power-delivery style) wired through ~100 nm nano-TSVs so both arrays share the same sense amps and decoders.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): sharing it across two arrays gives ~1.6-1.8x bits per wafer for one CMOS layer, reusing backside tools logic fabs are already buying.

title: Duplex-printed pillar: one vertical channel serves front and back cells
idea: Like printing both sides of a sheet, build each vertical pillar with a buried bitline contacting it at mid-height, an upper gate linking it to a front-side capacitor and a lower gate linking it to a backside capacitor formed after bonding and thinning, so one 4F2 footprint stores two bits.
why: Doubles bits per footprint to an effective 2F2 without extra lithographic tiers (fact 4) and halves bitline contacts per bit; risk is two independent gates on one short pillar.

title: Retinal light adaptation: sense references track hot cells' decay
idea: The retina adapts by referencing each photoreceptor to its neighbourhood average; in each 3D mat keep a few reference cells per row written with 1 and 0 alongside the data, and derive the sense reference from their live average so the threshold drifts down with the same temperature-driven leakage as the data cells.
why: At 125 C the '1' level decays fast toward a fixed mid-rail reference; an adaptive midpoint roughly doubles tolerated decay, doubling the refresh interval for <2% area.

title: Half-tone staircase: grayscale mask forms all tier steps at once
idea: Half-tone printing renders gray by dot density; use a sub-resolution dot grayscale reticle on an i-line/KrF stepper to form a stepped resist profile, then a proportional etch transfers all N staircase steps for a 3D array in one litho+etch instead of N trim-etch cycles.
why: Staircase cost and time scale with tier count (fact 2); one exposure on a depreciated scanner cuts staircase loops >10x for 32-64 tiers.

title: Planarian neoblast spare tiers adopt any failed tier's identity
idea: Build 4 'neoblast' spare tiers per 64-tier stack whose staircase is wired through an antifuse-programmable tier-address decoder; after test, any defective tier is disabled and a spare assumes its address, giving tier-level regeneration instead of only row/column repair.
why: 3D yield compounding: at 99% per-tier yield a 64-tier stack yields ~53%, with 4 spares >99%, roughly 1.8x lower effective cost per bit.

title: Eliminate the consumable wafer: foil arrays stacked like paper
idea: Build thin-film DRAM arrays on a reusable sapphire carrier, release each 2-5 um array foil by laser lift-off, and laminate dozens of foils into a stack with printed vertical vias; the carrier returns to the line hundreds of times.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: cuts Czochralski wafer (and Spruce Pine quartz crucible) consumption per bit by >10x and multiplies bits per footprint.

title: Swiss-roll DRAM: one planar array rolled into forty tiers
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality/curvature: build a single planar 1T1C array (thin trench capacitors) on a strained SiNx/Si bilayer over a sacrificial layer, then release it so the strip self-rolls into a 40-turn tube. All bitlines exit along the strip's leading edge, which stays flat and is hybrid-bonded to a logic die, so 40 effective tiers come from one mask set.
why: Fact 2 and 4: ~40x bits per litho pass without tier-by-tier processing; capital per bit could drop several-fold if roll registration, thermal path and contact yield can be solved.

title: Two-deck capacitor reusing one hole mask for AR 120
idea: Reverse 'one tall etch' into 'stack, etch, stack, etch': etch and line deck-1 capacitor holes, deposit a second mold deck, and re-expose the SAME capacitor mask aligned to deck 1 so deck-2 holes land on deck-1 electrodes, forming one continuous electrode. Zero new masks: one existing mask is used twice.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): reaches the AR ~115-120 needed for more charge using two AR-60 etches already in production, for ~1.6-1.8x Cs or a shrunken footprint.

title: Watchmaker's water drop: capillary self-aligned die-to-wafer hybrid bonding
idea: Make the bond sites hydrophilic and their surroundings hydrophobic, and dispense a water droplet on each site. A die dropped within +/-50 um self-centers to <0.5 um by surface tension as the water evaporates, then direct oxide/Cu bonding is annealed.
why: Memory-on-logic hybrid bonding with a ~$200k pick-and-place instead of a $5-10M precision bonder, within reach of a small team (Facts 5, 6).

title: Jelly-roll memory: one patterned film rolled into a thousand tiers
idea: IFR: 'a thousand tiers for the price of one.' Backward: pattern one long polyimide ribbon with oxide-TFT memory mats and an edge bus, then wind it like a battery jelly-roll; each turn's exposed edge bus lands on a laser-patterned end-cap whose radius-coded traces act as the vertical interconnect, like battery tabs.
why: 3D tier count and capital (fact 2, 4): tiers come from winding, not deposition or bonding; 1,000 turns of a 10 um film make a 1 cm cylinder.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores replace fluorocarbon-etched capacitor molds
idea: Substitute fluorocarbon-etched oxide molds with anodic aluminum oxide: sputter 3-5 um Al over storage pads, two-step anodize in oxalic/phosphoric acid to grow 25-35 nm hexagonal pores at AR >100:1, open the barrier by phosphoric-acid widening, fill with TiCl4-based ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN; pore diameter < inter-pad gap so no pore bridges two cells and each pad statistically lands several pores in parallel.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): AR 100-150 at bath-tool cost gives Cs ~8-12 fF with zero C4F6/C4F8 etch, no mold litho, abundant aluminum.

title: Sell tiers, not dies: overbuild tiers, fuse bad ones out
idea: Build early 3D DRAM with deliberately overprovisioned tiers (e.g. 40 built, 32 sold), test each tier through its own staircase contact, and map defective tiers out with tier-level fuses. This reverses the yield model from 'one defect kills the die' to 'a defect costs one tier'.
why: 3D break-even (fact 2): lifting die yield from ~40% to >90% for immature processes at 25% extra tier cost cuts cost per good bit ~45%, pulling 3D in years earlier.

title: Thermally drawn multimaterial fibers woven like core planes into memory
idea: Revive hand-woven core planes with fiber drawing: a macroscopic preform holding metal, dielectric and semiconductor features is drawn ~1000x down into kilometers of fiber with ~50-100 nm internal cell structures, then fibers are woven or bundled and sliced into dense 3D arrays. Patterning happens once in the preform, not per wafer.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: no EUV or per-wafer masks, built in fiber plants; cost per bit could drop >3x if drawn features stay uniform.

title: Organ builder's tuned pipes: frequency-addressed tier selection
idea: An organ selects a pipe by its pitch. Give each tier a thin-film bulk-acoustic resonator whose frequency is set by that tier's own film thickness. One shared RF tier bus carries a tone, and only the matching tier's resonator rectifies it to turn on its select gates.
why: Replaces the staircase contact region and N tier decoders, which grow with tier count in 3D (Facts 2, 7).

title: Ham radio operator's near-field link: coil-coupled stack without TSVs
idea: Ham operators talk without wires. Put 30-60 um inductive coils in the top metal of every die, glue thinned dies into a stack, and send data die-to-die by near-field magnetic coupling at ~1-8 Gb/s per coil and ~0.1-1 pJ/bit. Power comes in on edge wire bonds, and the design can be taped out on an MPW.
why: Avoids the HBM TSV area and yield tax (Fact 6) and moves data at under 1 pJ/bit (Fact 5), with packaging a small team can do.

title: National open 3D-DRAM pilot line fused with shared PDK at Albany
idea: Combine the Albany NY public R&D fab with an open, licensable 3D-DRAM process design kit: startups and universities tape out cell and array variants on shared multi-project wafers, and CHIPS money buys tier-stack and bonding tool sets whose recipes transfer to US production fabs.
why: Capital and time (fact 4): entry cost for a new US memory architecture drops from ~$1B to ~$1-5M per experiment, speeding the 3D cell search (fact 2).

title: Charge-coupled pillar: vertical shift-register DRAM, no capacitor
idea: Reverse 3D NAND's vertical string: store charge packets under each word-tier gate of an oxide-semiconductor channel pillar and clock them up the pillar CCD-style (three-phase gates) to one sense node at the top, so each pillar is a 64-bit vertical shift register with no per-bit transistor or capacitor.
why: Capacitor wall and 3D cell (facts 1,2): bit = one gate tier x pillar pitch on a 3D NAND-like line; IGZO's low leakage gives ms retention; ~1 ns/stage keeps a 64-bit block read under ~100 ns; charge has unlimited endurance.

title: Vertical CCD memory: charge buckets shifted down gate-stacked pillars
idea: [Box: charge packets in channel potential wells | no access transistor, clocked word-plates | floating-diffusion sense at pillar base | 3D-NAND-like plate stack | Si or IGZO channel | blanket plate deposition + one hole etch] Each tier plate is a CCD gate around a vertical channel; three-phase clocking shifts packets down to one sense node at the base and recirculates them to the top, turning each hole into a 64-128-bit rotating shift register.
why: No 3D cell (fact 2) and periphery (fact 7): no capacitor or transistor per bit and one sense node per hole; ~64 ns per 64-bit burst suits row-buffer-style access, ~3-5x DRAM density.

title: Nano-velcro reworkable stacking: unhook and replace bad tiers
idea: Template-electroplate copper nanowire hook fields on stack pads in existing bump lines so mating fields interlock at room temperature like Velcro; test the stack, peel off any bad die, press in a good one, then anneal to make the joints permanent.
why: Turns the 20-30% HBM stack yield loss (fact 6) into a repairable step, so stack yield approaches die yield, with no bonding thermal budget.

title: Hydrogen ion-slice stacking of 32 single-crystal silicon tiers
idea: Implant H+ into a pre-doped donor Si wafer, oxide-bond it onto the growing stack at <=350 C, cleave at the hydrogen plane, CMP, pattern only the lateral access transistors, and repeat ~32 times, reusing each donor ~10x; all capacitors are then formed by one vertical etch through every tier.
why: Removes the 3D-DRAM lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) by giving every tier bulk-grade mobility and a tight leakage tail (fact 3), without the strain limit of Si/SiGe epi stacks; targets 26+ crystalline tiers and ~3-4x bits per wafer vs planar 1z.

title: Molybdenum wordlines double as in-field annealing heaters
idea: Combine the wordline with a micro-heater: during maintenance windows, pulse current through domestic Mo buried wordlines (replacing Chinese tungsten) to Joule-heat a mat to ~250 C for milliseconds to seconds, annealing hydrogen-related interface traps behind variable-retention-time leakage and weak cells.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): shrinking the <=13 fA tail could double or more the refresh interval (refresh energy halved) and heal hammer-induced trap damage (fact 9); thermal stress on neighbors is the risk.

title: Leakage-ratioed loadless pair holds state across two tiers
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: build a true/complement storage-node pair across two tiers with cross-coupled access devices whose off-state leakage is pre-engineered (Vt, length) to be ~10x stronger toward the rail each node already sits at. Leakage then holds the state like a loadless 4T SRAM instead of erasing it.
why: Fact 3: refresh eliminated (-16-33% idle power, +10-20% bandwidth) at 2x transistor count, but two-tier stacking keeps the footprint near 1T1C; no capacitor.

title: Backside-etched capacitors through thinned wafer free 4F² footprint
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor sits on top of the bitline (COB).' Build vertical-channel transistors and bitlines on the front side, bond to a carrier, thin the wafer to ~1.5 um and etch the capacitors from the back side so they land directly on each transistor's buried drain; capacitor and bitline contact stop competing for the same face.
why: Facts 1 and 4: enables true 4F² (33% less area than 6F²) and lets capacitor height come from a separate backside module instead of a 70:1 front-side etch threaded between contacts.

title: Eliminate sacrificial SiGe: Si/CaF2 epitaxial insulator superlattice
idea: Grow 3D DRAM tiers as an epitaxial superlattice of silicon and lattice-matched CaF2 (~0.6% mismatch), so the inter-tier insulator is grown in its final form and no sacrificial layer needs wet lateral removal and refill.
why: Water: removes the wet lateral SiGe recess, its rinses, and the refill/etch-back cycles of 3D DRAM tier formation; helps reach 26+ tiers with ~10x fewer wet steps per bit.

title: Minify front-side clutter: move 4F2 bitlines to wafer backside
idea: In a vertical-channel 4F2 cell, form the bitlines on the backside after wafer thinning to about 300 nm, contacting the bottom of each vertical channel, as backside power delivery does. The front side is then free for a full-height capacitor, and the buried-bitline coupling and resistance problem goes away.
why: Makes 4F2 manufacturable: 33% less area than 6F2, lower BL-BL coupling (about 30% less sense noise), and a wider BL metal (about 3x lower resistance).

title: Vertical bitline pillar with built-in preamp transistor at its base
idea: Merge the local sense preamp into each vertical bitline of a 3D DRAM: a gain transistor whose gate is the short vertical bitline converts the charge-share signal to current before it reaches the long global bitline.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): with ~0.2 fF vertical bitline, a 1 fF cell transfers ~83% of its signal, so cells need ~1 fF instead of 5 fF; enables short lateral capacitors and 100+ tiers (fact 2).

title: Hexagonal block-copolymer holes for vertical oxide-channel rings
idea: Under 400 C, cylinder-forming block copolymer annealed at 250 C self-assembles a 28 nm-pitch hexagonal hole lattice. Each hole gets an ALD ring channel and gate-all-around wordline, giving an EUV-free vertical cell array.
why: Fact 4: sub-30 nm pitch with no EUV and about 15% hex-packing gain; cell masks drop from 5-7 EUV to 1 ArF guide pattern.

title: Drip irrigation: ground-precharged bitlines with sparsity-maximizing encoding
idea: Water only the plants that need it: precharge bitlines to 0 V instead of VDD/2 and store each 64-bit word in whichever polarity has fewer ones (plus a flag bit), paired with zero-skewed tensor formats, so only bitlines that read a 1 draw charge.
why: Bitline energy proportional to ones (facts 8, 10): with ReLU/quantized tensors at 5-15% ones after encoding, claims 5-10x lower bitline energy per access.

title: Buried back-gate plane per tier: negative hold bias, low-swing wordlines
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor threshold is fixed.' Give every tier a doped-Si back-gate plane under its channels, biased strongly negative during hold to raise Vt and crush leakage, then relaxed per bank on access, so wordlines swing ~1.5 V instead of ~3 V.
why: Facts 3 and 10: leakage tail cut ~10-100x and wordline CV² energy ~4x lower, with Si only.

title: Billboard painter's giant canvas: idle display fabs print memory panels
idea: A billboard painter works big and coarse. A 10-person team designs oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays for idle Gen-6 display lines. A 1.5 m2 panel at 1.5 um rules holds ~5e10 bits (~6 GB), and it is diced into tiles bonded to logic as a slow bulk tier.
why: Uses paid-off, non-EUV display capacity for bulk working memory. Cost is projected at ~$30/GB today, falling with tighter display rules (capital, scarce EUV).

title: Eliminate TSVs: shingled stacks with laser-written edge interconnect
idea: Stack dies offset like roof shingles so each die's pad row is exposed, then write vertical interconnect down the stepped edge with laser direct-write or aerosol-jet silver, with no TSV etch, liner, copper plating or reveal.
why: Water and TSV tax: the TSV module (etch, wet clean, ECD, reveal CMP) is the most water-heavy part of HBM; removing it gives ~10x lower stacking water and recovers the keep-out area.

title: Eliminate TSVs: through-silicon optical links at 1310 nm
idea: Silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so stacked thinned dies talk vertically through the bulk with micro-LED or VCSEL emitters and Ge photodiodes aligned in columns, with no drilled or plated vias.
why: Water and HBM tax: no TSV etch, wet clean, ECD or reveal CMP, and no keep-out zones; each optical column can carry tens of Gb/s.

title: Mirror-twin tiers interleave bitlines so the idle twin provides reference
idea: Fabricate tiers in mirrored pairs above and below one shared bitline layer whose lines alternate between serving the top tier and the bottom tier; when the top tier fires, each neighbouring bitline belongs to the idle bottom tier and acts as a perfectly matched reference.
why: Recovers folded-bitline noise rejection (~2x effective signal) inside a 4F^2 open geometry, lowering required Cs (fact 1), and halves bitline layers and sense-amp rows per tier pair (fact 7) at no area cost.

title: Depreciated U.S. 200-mm fabs become array-tier foundries
idea: Use the decades-old installed base as capacity: about a dozen U.S. 200-mm fabs at 180-350 nm run array-only tier wafers in the sideways architecture, with no periphery, die-to-wafer bonded to periphery made elsewhere. Contracts are priced per tier, not per die.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital (fact 4; U.S. makes 1-2% of DRAM): mobilizes existing fabs in ~1-2 years with near-zero new capex.

title: Tungsten-free TiN wordlines stitched to Cu every 128 cells
idea: Reverse the wordline's job: buried TiN-only lines just gate the cells, while a copper strap above carries the current, connected every 128 cells through one added stitch-contact mask. RC falls ~16x, which covers TiN's ~4x higher resistivity.
why: Scarce resources (China ~80% of tungsten): removes tungsten from the array's largest use; U.S. supply resilience.

title: Capacitive tier vias: AC-coupled signaling with no metal plugs
idea: Inverts 'tier-to-tier connections need metal vias (W plugs).' Separate tiers by thin SiN and pass signals through overlapping Al pads acting as ~1-5 fF coupling capacitors driven by pulse-mode transceivers, with power on a few large Al vias.
why: Fact 6 and W chokepoint: no TSVs or W plugs, and tiers bond without fine metal-to-metal alignment.

title: Spiral-wound memory foil around a silicon logic spindle
idea: Wind a 10 m x 5 cm printed DRAM foil around a 1 cm logic core like a film capacitor, Schoop-spray metal onto the roll's end faces for power and plate, and route signals to pads along the foil's top edge, which land in a spiral pattern mated by an end cap.
why: Volumetric first principle: 0.5 m^2 of 25 um foil at ~60 GB/m^2 fits in a ~2.2 cm-diameter roll (~30 GB) with every cell within 2.5 cm of an end face (printed Ag line RC ~60 ps), giving capacity with no stacking tools.

title: Low-temperature ferroelectric tier licensing for idle US logic fabs
idea: Low-temperature orthorhombic-phase crystallization: HZO and AlScN become ferroelectric at ≤400 C, so non-volatile memory tiers can be added on top of finished logic wafers. A business would license a 'memory-tier kit' (process recipe, compiler, test IP) to US 28-65 nm fabs, turning underused capacity into memory output without a new DRAM fab.
why: Attacks US manufacturability (1-2% share) and capital intensity (fact 4); claim memory output at <10% of greenfield DRAM capex per wafer.

title: Metal-induced lateral crystallization from bitline holes seeds all tiers
idea: Worse: accept leaky poly channels in deposited tiers or pay for 200 epitaxial or bonded layers. Flip: deposit cheap a-Si tiers, drop a Ni or Al nucleant into the vertical bitline holes, and anneal at ~500 C so crystallization fronts grow laterally from each hole along every tier at once, giving near-single-grain channels exactly where the access transistors sit, then strip the nucleant.
why: Near-crystalline leakage tails (fact 3) at deposited-film cost from one anneal, so 100-200 cheap tiers deliver 10x density at roughly 2D wafer cost; metal contamination control is the risk.

title: Veneer slicing: deposit layers, slice block, get 10 nm lines
idea: Borrowed from wood-veneer slicing and nanoskiving: deposit 500 alternating 10 nm metal/oxide layers as a thick block, slice it perpendicular with a diamond microtome into thin slabs, and lay the slabs flat so the cut face exposes 10 nm lines whose pitch is set by deposition, not litho; cross two slabs for a crosspoint array.
why: Sub-10 nm wordline/bitline gratings without EUV (fact 4), patterning cost ~1/100; trade-offs: slab registration, needs a crosspoint-compatible gain cell or selector.

title: Eliminate interlayer dielectric fill: vacuum-gap array wiring
idea: Leave the space between bitlines, wordlines and tiers as sealed vacuum cavities (pinch-off cap deposition) instead of gap-fill oxide followed by CMP, with nitride posts holding the structure.
why: Water and charge wall: no gap-fill CMP or its cleans, and bitline capacitance falls ~2x, so a ~2x smaller Cs gives the same signal and relaxes capacitor AR.

title: Thermos flask: sealed vacuum gaps around vertical bitlines
idea: Like a vacuum flask, after the 3D stack is built, selectively remove a sacrificial carbon or SiGe interlayer between vertical bitlines and wordline plates and pinch it shut with a non-conformal cap, replacing k ~4 fill with vacuum.
why: Bitline capacitance and voltage floor (facts 8, 10): Cb ~3x lower lets Cs shrink 3x at the same transfer ratio, and lower coupling allows VARY ~0.6 V; claims ~3x x ~3x = ~9-10x lower energy per access.

title: Thermos flask: sealed vacuum gaps between wordlines block hammer coupling
idea: A thermos insulates with vacuum: after the buried wordlines are formed, recess the isolation dielectric between passing wordlines and neighbor active areas and seal it with a pinch-off cap, leaving vacuum gaps (k=1). Capacitive kick and charge migration from aggressor to victim fall, and the DDR5/HBM interface is untouched.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): coupling ~3x lower, aiming at a 3-5x higher flip threshold; lower wordline capacitance also trims wordline CV2 energy (fact 10).

title: Setun balanced-ternary charge in 3D cells around the half-VDD plate
idea: Revive the Soviet Setun ternary computer: each 3D cell holds negative, zero or positive charge relative to the existing VDD/2 plate (1.58 bits/cell), read by a two-threshold sense amp; the narrowed margin causes ~1% level confusions, absorbed by a ternary BCH code over GF(3).
why: Density: +58% bits per tier without extra layers or taller capacitors; ~45% net after code overhead.

title: Loom weaver's crosspoint: selector-capacitor cell at every thread crossing
idea: A weaver puts a knot at every warp-weft crossing. Build stackable crosspoint decks in which each crossing holds a back-to-back ovonic threshold selector in series with a thin MIM capacitor (1S1C). There is no access transistor, and holding the half-select bias minimises selector leakage during retention.
why: Each deck is 4F2 and is stacked like 3D XPoint, with no lateral transistor, the blocker named in Fact 2; ~4x density at 4 decks, if selector off-leakage can be pushed below ~10 fA.

title: Substrate-free van der Waals stack with nanometer-thin memory tiers
idea: IFR: 'each tier is a few molecules thick.' Backward: grow wafer-scale MoS2 channels and hBN dielectrics on reusable sapphire and dry-transfer them tier by tier, so each cell layer (2D channel, hBN, metal gate) is ~5 nm and 100 tiers fit in 0.5 um while the sapphire is reused.
why: 3D tiers and leakage (facts 2, 3): MoS2's ~1.8 eV gap gives very low off-current, and a ~20x thinner tier pitch keeps vertical etches shallow.

title: SAGE-style federal anchor order for error-tolerant U.S. memory stacks
idea: SAGE's huge core-memory order drove core prices down ~100x and built U.S. core factories; revive it as a multiyear federal purchase commitment for 'grade-T' 3D memory specified at up to 1% raw cell BER with on-stack correction, made in U.S. mature-node fabs.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: guaranteed volume justifies cheaper tolerant fabs without EUV, raising domestic share from ~1-2%.

title: Swiss roll: strained nanomembranes self-roll into capacitor scrolls
idea: A Swiss roll packs a long sheet into a small volume: deposit a planar TiN/HZO/TiN/HZO multilayer on a strained SiGe/Si bilayer in each lateral 3D cell, then release it with a selective etch so it curls into a 4-5 turn scroll inside the cell recess. Plate area grows with sheet length rather than etch depth.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2): flat lateral capacitors give <1 fF; scrolls could give 5-10 fF in a 200 nm recess.

title: Doping-selective porous-silicon anodization carves all tier cavities at once
idea: Use a wafer-scale electrochemical bath on every tier in one step: grow alternating p+/p- silicon layers in a 1990s epi reactor, open one 180-nm slot, and anodize. Only the p+ layers turn porous and dissolve, leaving lateral cavities for capacitors and gates in every tier at once, with no SiGe and no high-AR selective dry etch.
why: Lateral-cavity formation is a key 3D DRAM blocker (fact 2): one wet step replaces a lateral etch per tier, cheap and U.S.-manufacturable.

title: Minify sense-amp offset by trimming each amp after fab
idea: Add a fuse- or antifuse-programmed binary capacitor trim to every sense-amp pair, set during wafer test, to cancel measured offset below 5 mV. Prove it on a 28 nm MPW and license to second-tier DRAM makers.
why: Charge wall: smaller offset allows about 30% smaller Cs or lower VARY. The IP plus test chip fits in $1M.

title: Seven-track tape parity rebuilt as a physical 3D product code
idea: Revive 1950s tape drives' lateral-plus-longitudinal parity: one parity tier per 16 tiers plus parity pillars per row put every bit in row, column and tier codewords, decoded iteratively to correct 1% scattered cell errors along all three axes.
why: Facts 2 and 9: corrects at 1% raw BER with ~15-20% overhead while localizing wordline shorts and row-hammer bursts.

title: MLCC-style multi-plate lateral capacitor for 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Copy multilayer-ceramic-capacitor construction: inside each tier's lateral capacitor recess, ALD 2N alternating TiN/high-k layers, then open one vertical slit where odd plates are recessed on one side and even plates on the other (like MLCC end terminations), so all plates connect in parallel between storage node and plate line.
why: The lateral capacitor blocks 3D DRAM (fact 2); parallel plates give Cs proportional to plate count instead of recess length, so 4 plate pairs cut lateral cell length ~4x, shrinking cell pitch and lowering the ~26-tier break-even.

title: Keep the sacrificial SiGe as hole-storage wells in each tier
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: 3D DRAM flows grow Si/SiGe superlattices and then spend effort removing the SiGe; instead keep a thin SiGe layer under each Si channel as a valence-band quantum well. Holes written by impact ionization or GIDL sit in the well and shift the overlying channel's Vt via body effect, giving a capacitorless 1T cell in every tier.
why: Fact 1 and 2: removes both 3D blockers (capacitor and its lateral integration); ~4F2 per tier and the ~0.2-0.3 eV band offset could extend floating-body retention ~10-100x.

title: Avalanche-gain segment amplifies charge at each vertical bitline
idea: Impact ionization: a short vertical p-i-n avalanche section at the foot of each vertical bitline multiplies the charge dumped by a tiny tier capacitor 50-100x before it reaches the sense amp. It works like an avalanche photodiode, but for stored electrons.
why: Lets 3D tiers use 10x smaller capacitors (facts 1 and 2) and shrinks sense-amp periphery (fact 7); claim 10x Cs relief, with excess noise the main risk.

title: Optical-disc error correction lets arrays ship with 1% dead cells
idea: Borrowed from CDs and Blu-ray, which ship with defects and rely on interleaved Reed-Solomon/LDPC: design arrays with soft-decision sensing and ~25% parity so up to 1% dead or weak-retention cells are absorbed, eliminating laser repair and per-cell screening.
why: The enabler that makes 100x-cheap processes (panels, imprint, 200+ tiers) sellable: effective yield on 100-tier stacks rises from ~30% to ~95%, a ~3x lever inside the 100x stack-up.

title: Submariner's bulkheads: grounded shield tiers isolate hammer coupling
idea: Submarines compartmentalize so one flood does not sink the boat. Interleave a 3 nm grounded conductive bulkhead film between active tiers, and grounded shield fins between adjacent lateral wordlines in 3D DRAM.
why: Cuts wordline-to-wordline and tier-to-tier capacitive coupling and trap-mediated disturb, aiming at a row hammer threshold above 10k activations (Fact 9). Costs one deposition per tier.

title: Dendritic-spine cells sprout sideways from one vertical bitline shaft
idea: Each vertical bitline is a dendrite shaft; at every tier a selective SiGe recess in a Si/SiGe superlattice leaves a thin 'spine neck' nanowire channel gated by that tier's wordline plane, ending in a bulbous 'spine head' storage node lined by ALD dielectric, so a 64-tier cell column is made from a single hole.
why: No manufacturable 3D cell: self-aligned per-tier transistor+capacitor from one etch; the narrow neck gives high off-resistance; aims at 3D break-even near 30 tiers with 2-3 critical masks per 64 tiers.

title: Progressive-JPEG bit-plane tiers: fetch only the precision needed
idea: Progressive JPEG sends coarse bits first; store each tensor element's bits across separate 3D tiers (MSB plane, next plane, and so on) so a pass needing 4-bit precision activates 4 of 16 bit-plane rows, and MSB-plane zeros mask whole lower-plane fetches.
why: Precision overfetch (facts 5, 8): bits activated and moved per useful value drop 4x, toward ~10x with MSB-gated skipping; claims ~10x lower energy per AI access.

title: Cellular frequency reuse: four-color tier activation shares drivers
idea: Adapted from cellular frequency-reuse coloring: tiers and subarrays are assigned four 'colors' and neighboring same-color regions never activate together, so one wordline-driver bank serves four tiers in rotation and aggressor rows are never adjacent to active victims.
why: Wordline driver count ~4x lower in 3D stacks (fact 7) and inter-tier row-hammer coupling bounded by construction (fact 9).

title: Naturally layered crystal grows the 3D tier stack itself
idea: Po: chips are grown like minerals, not built. Epitaxially grow a Ruddlesden-Popper layered oxide whose unit cell alternates a semiconducting perovskite sheet with an insulating rock-salt spacer, so one PLD/MBE growth yields hundreds of perfectly registered channel/dielectric tiers; gate and bitline holes are then etched vertically through the crystal.
why: Fact 2: hundreds of superlattice deposition steps collapse into one epitaxy; atomically flat spacers give near-identical Vt in every tier.

title: Area-selective ALD grows tier-to-tier vias bottom-up
idea: Under 400 C, Ru grows by area-selective ALD only on exposed Ru landing pads, not on the surrounding dielectric, at 300 C. Each new tier's contacts self-align upward with no via lithography.
why: Fact 4: removes one critical mask per tier in monolithic stacks, about 30% fewer litho steps over 32 tiers.

title: Noise-cancelling headphones: replica-bitline subtraction enables tiny signals
idea: Like ANC headphones playing anti-noise, give every 8 bitlines a cell-less replica bitline that sees the same wordline kick and neighbour coupling; the sense amp subtracts it in the charge domain, so 30 mV signals become reliable and VARY drops to ~0.4 V.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): 1.0 to 0.4 V gives ~6x on CV2, and the smaller required signal allows ~1.5x smaller Cs; claims ~8-10x lower array energy.

title: Self-timed tiers: replica bitlines replace global worst-case timing
idea: Inverts 'the array runs to one synchronous timing spec.' Each tier/subarray carries a replica bitline whose sense completion fires a ready signal, so fast tiers return data early and slow tiers no longer set tRCD for the whole stack or cause scrap.
why: Facts 2 and 4: tier-to-tier variation in 3D becomes latency variance instead of yield loss; ~15-30% average latency gain and higher stack yield.

title: Minify speed to 1 us: 2-bit cells with shared ramp sensing
idea: Build a deliberately slow far-memory tier with 1 us access: cells store 2 bits (4 charge levels), and 64 bitlines share one slow, precise ramp-ADC sense circuit, time-multiplexed.
why: Cost per bit: 2x bits per cell and 64x fewer sense amps, for tiered memory holding cold KV-cache and pages at about 40-50% lower cost per bit.

title: Anodized aluminum pores self-assemble the capacitor forest without etch
idea: Borrowed from architectural aluminum anodizing: sputter 3 um of Al over the access-transistor array, imprint shallow dimples at cell sites, and anodize so hexagonal pores self-align to them at ~100:1 aspect ratio; line the pores with TiN/high-k/TiN to form every capacitor without plasma etch or EUV.
why: A wet bath replaces the hardest high-AR etch module and its masks (facts 1,4), capacitor module cost ~-95%; with a relaxed ~30 nm EUV-free periphery it is a core piece of a 100x cost path.

title: Shaker minimalist: two-mask thyristor crosspoint on purchased epi wafers
idea: The Shaker craftsman removes every unnecessary step. Buy wafers with an in-situ-doped p+/n/p/n+ epi stack from a vendor, etch line mask 1, fill, then etch perpendicular line mask 2, leaving self-aligned 4F2 thyristor pillars. Each pillar is a bistable latch with ns read and write.
why: No capacitor and no access transistor, built in a university fab with two masks; epi decks can be bonded into stacks (Facts 1, 2, 4). Holding-current standby is the cost.

title: Subarray sense amps fused with micro-ring optical modulators
idea: Bond a photonic wafer over the DRAM array so every subarray's local sense-amp row drives silicon micro-ring modulators directly; the latched bit biases the ring's PN junction, and global bitlines, I/O muxes and SERDES become one WDM waveguide bus running over the mats.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and overfetch (fact 8): claimed <1 pJ/bit array-to-processor versus 3-4 pJ/bit HBM, and bank-level parallel optical channels.

title: Phased-array radar timing: colliding pulses select the wordline segment
idea: Borrowed from radar/ultrasound beam steering: a long tier wordline is driven as a transmission line from both ends with two sub-threshold pulses timed to superpose above threshold only at the target segment, selecting it without any per-segment decoder.
why: Deletes local wordline decoders and drivers in 3D stacks (fact 7, periphery ~49%), periphery area ~-30%; requires ps-level timing control.
